title: Dictionary.com’s 2026 word, maxxing, is a word chunk set free, like -holic and -gate
body: On 25 October 2026 Dictionary.com [named](https://www.dictionary.com/articles/word-of-the-year-2026) maxxing its Word of the Year: the practice of pursuing an activity to the fullest, as in looksmaxxing or tokenmaxxing, using as much AI at work as possible. It grew from max and the gamers’ term min-maxing: other words took the place of min, and maxing, which picked up an extra x, became an ending that sticks onto almost anything. Linguists call a freed-up piece like this a [libfix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libfix), a term coined by Arnold Zwicky in 2010. The trick is to cut a well-known word in a new place and hear the leftover piece as carrying the meaning: alcoholic is alcohol plus -ic, yet it gave -holic and workaholic, first recorded in 1947; the Watergate scandal of 1972 left -gate; walkathon, from 1932, freed -athon. Some pieces end up standing alone, as burger did from hamburger, and in 2026 maxxing began to as well.

slides.question: In what year did a newspaper first print the word workaholic, as far as the Oxford English Dictionary knows?
slides.explanation: 1947, in the Toronto Daily Star: work plus the -holic cut from alcoholic. The same ending has since given shopaholic and more.

slides.prompt: Tap between two letters to cut each word where English cut it to free a new ending. Find all five cuts.
slides.takeaway: Alco|holic, Water|gate, mar|athon, ham|burger, min-|maxing. The cut is often not where the word’s own parts meet: alcoholic is alcohol + ic, hamburger is Hamburg + er.

slides.heading: Same words, two ways to cut them

left.label: Their own parts
left.text: alcohol + ic. Hamburg + er. Marathon, a place name in Greece. Min-maxing, a gaming strategy.

right.label: How English reused them
right.text: work-a-holic, shop-a-holic. Cheese-burger, then burger alone. Walk-athon, hack-athon. Looksmaxxing, then maxxing alone.

slides.heading: Who’s maxxing?
slides.text: Dictionary.com says looksmaxxing, about appearance, arose on Reddit and other forums, with evidence back to 2015, and that its early users were largely young men. In 2026 the pattern spread to work, wellness and jokes: cozymaxxing can mean a night in with snacks. Also shortlisted: affordability, odyssey, unc.

slides.question: According to Dictionary.com, which gaming term helped give English the word maxxing?
slides.explanation: Min-maxing means building up a character’s strengths until its weaknesses no longer matter. Other words took the place of min, and maxing became an ending of its own.
